title: A finite local subsystem generates a finite torsion subgroup subsystem
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-etale-site], assume the underlying set sheaf of $G$ is a local system [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system], and assume every element of every geometric stalk is killed by a positive integer [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. If $E\hookrightarrow G$ is a finite locally constant subsheaf of sets, then there is a finite locally constant abelian subgroup sheaf $H\hookrightarrow G$ containing $E$. Here finite locally constant means etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite set (for $E$) or a finite abelian group (for $H$) [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301, and the finite local subgroup systems used implicitly in Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303; agent-formulated auxiliary consequence, not a separately stated lemma in the source.

proof.text: The connected components $X_c$ of the Noetherian space $X$ are finitely many open and closed subspaces. Regard them as open subschemes. Restriction of $G$ to $X_c$ is still a set local system by pullback stability; restriction of $E$ is finite locally constant by its defining trivializations, and stalkwise torsion is unchanged. It suffices to construct the required subgroup on each nonempty $X_c$. The empty scheme is dealt with by its unique abelian sheaf. We work on one component until Step 7.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: Choose a geometric point $x$ of this nonempty connected component and put $\Pi=\pi_1(X_c,x)$. The set-monodromy equivalence identifies $G$ with a discrete continuous $\Pi$-set $A=G_x$. The inclusion $E\hookrightarrow G$ corresponds to an inclusion of $\Pi$-sets $S\hookrightarrow A$: equivalences preserve finite limits, the local-system category computes them in ambient sheaves, and a map is monic precisely when its kernel-pair diagonal is an isomorphism. The finite-etale representability theorem makes $E$ a finite etale representable, so the finite-fibre clause of the set-monodromy equivalence makes $S$ finite. Products and terminal objects of set local systems are ambient products and terminal objects. Their universal properties and sectionwise limits show that the addition, zero and inverse of $G$ induce the usual abelian-group operations on $A$. Naturality of monodromy for these three maps says $\gamma(a+b)=\gamma a+\gamma b$, $\gamma 0=0$, and $\gamma(-a)=-\gamma a$; thus every $\gamma\in\Pi$ acts by a group automorphism.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: List the finite subset $S$ as $s_1,\ldots,s_r$, and choose $n_i>0$ with $n_i s_i=0$ using the torsion hypothesis on $G_x$. Define $B=\{\sum_{i=1}^r a_i s_i:a_i\in\mathbf Z\}\subset A$. It is an abelian subgroup containing $S$. Reducing each coefficient modulo $n_i$ shows that every element of $B$ is one of the finitely many sums with $0\leq a_i<n_i$, so $B$ is finite. Also $N=\prod_i n_i>0$ annihilates $B$. For $S=\varnothing$ use $B=\{0\}$ and $N=1$. This proves the finite-generation torsion calculation directly, without using a structure theorem.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: The image $S$ of the equivariant map $E_x\to G_x$ is $\Pi$-invariant. For $\gamma\in\Pi$, the group-automorphism identities of Step 2 give $\gamma(\sum_i a_i s_i)=\sum_i a_i\gamma(s_i)\in B$. Applying the same argument to $\gamma^{-1}$ gives $\gamma B=B$. Thus $B\hookrightarrow A$ and $S\to B$ are equivariant maps. The stabilizer of $b\in B$ for the restricted action is exactly its stabilizer in $A$, which is open; hence $B$ with its discrete topology is a continuous finite $\Pi$-set. Its addition, inverse and zero are equivariant because they are restrictions of those of $A$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: Apply the finite fundamental-group equivalence to the finite continuous $\Pi$-set $B$. It supplies a finite etale representable $H_0$ whose fibre is $B$, equivariantly; its underlying set sheaf is finite locally constant by finite-etale representability. The agreement of the set-monodromy equivalence with the finite fibre functor identifies its image with $B$. Fullness therefore lifts $B\hookrightarrow A$, $S\to B$, and the equivariant maps $B\times B\to B$, $B\to B$, and $\{*\}\to B$ to sheaf maps $j:H_0\to G$, $E\to H_0$, addition, inverse, and zero. Here finite products are ambient products by the local-system calculus, and their fibre identifications follow from preservation of limits by the equivalence. Faithfulness verifies each abelian-group identity, the homomorphism identities for $j$, and equality of $E\to H_0\to G$ with the given inclusion, because their fibre maps have those identities. Finally $B\hookrightarrow A$ has an isomorphic kernel-pair diagonal, so preservation of ambient finite limits and reflection of isomorphisms give the same for $j$. Thus $j$ is monic in ambient set sheaves. With the lifted group operations $H_0$ is an abelian subgroup sheaf $H\hookrightarrow G$ containing $E$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: Faithfulness of the set-monodromy equivalence also gives $N\,\mathrm{id}_H=0$, since this holds on $B$. Therefore repeated addition equips $H$ with a sheaf structure over the finite ring $\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$: the residue class of $a$ acts by $h\mapsto ah$, independently of the representative since $NH=0$. Apply the finite-underlying-module local-constancy theorem to this module sheaf. Its only additional hypotheses are that the coefficient ring is finite and that the underlying set sheaf is finite locally constant, both verified above. It supplies an etale cover on which $H$ is the constant sheaf of a module. Forgetting scalars in these trivializations gives constant abelian sheaves; the module values are finite because their underlying constant sheaves have the finite geometric stalks $B$. Hence $H$ is finite locally constant as an abelian sheaf, as required.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 7.2.3, p. 301; explicit finite subgroup construction supporting Lemma 7.2.6, p. 303.

proof.text: Perform Steps 2--6 separately on every $X_c$, obtaining $H_c\hookrightarrow G|_{X_c}$. For an etale $U\to X$, define $H(U)$ to be the subgroup of $G(U)$ consisting of those sections whose restrictions to every $U\times_X X_c$ lie in $H_c(U\times_X X_c)$. This is a sheaf: compatible local sections glue uniquely in $G$, and membership in each $H_c$ can be checked on the induced covering because $H_c$ is a subsheaf. It is closed under addition and inverse and contains zero, componentwise. It contains $E$ and restricts to $H_c$ on $X_c$. The trivializing etale covers for the $H_c$, composed with the open inclusions $X_c\to X$, cover $X$ and trivialize $H$ as a finite abelian sheaf. This gives the asserted global subgroup, including the empty case.
